research_question: Can alternative optimal transport costs improve non-rigid shape correspondence?

papers.title: Deep Shells: Unsupervised Shape Correspondence with Optimal Transport
Integrating Efficient Optimal Transport and Functional Maps For Unsupervised Shape Correspondence Learning

findings.statement: Entropy-regularized OT energy integrating squared product-embedding distance enables differentiable Sinkhorn-based shape matching.
findings.evidence: Eq. 8: OT energy integrating squared embedding distance under pi minus entropy regularization enables differentiable Sinkhorn optimization

findings.statement: Pairwise OT ground cost is explicitly encoded as Gibbs density from negative scaled squared embedding distance.
findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines p_lambda as exponential of negative scaled squared distance for Sinkhorn input

findings.statement: A second OT energy using learned feature distance computes initial soft correspondences, exemplifying an alternative ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 13: OT energy using learned feature distance to compute initial pi, showing alternative ground cost in same pipeline

findings.statement: Product-space embedding of intrinsic eigenfunctions and extrinsic coordinates/normals defines the space where Euclidean distance serves as OT ground cost.
findings.evidence: Eq. 3 embeds shape X into R^{K+6} using intrinsic eigenfunctions plus extrinsic smoothed coordinates and normals whose Euclidean distance becomes ground cost

findings.statement: Bidirectional sliced Wasserstein OT loss aligning feature distributions improves correspondence compared to MSE baseline.
findings.evidence: Eq. 10 defines bidirectional SW loss; Table 4 ablation shows replacing BiSW/EBSW with MSE degrades drastically (Table 4, Eq. 10)

findings.statement: Bidirectional energy-based sliced Wasserstein with shared slicing distribution provides a more discriminative alternative OT cost than uniform slicing.
findings.evidence: Eq. 6 defines energy-weighted slicing; Eq. 11 defines bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution claimed to improve over uniform SW (Eq. 6, Eq. 11)

findings.statement: Test-time adaptive refinement via entropic OT Sinkhorn projections improves final point maps.
findings.evidence: Eq. 14 defines iterated Sinkhorn projections for entropic OT plan; ablation reports error 4.7 to 7.2 without refinement (Eq. 14, Table 4)

findings.statement: Sliced Wasserstein offers O(n log n) time and O(n) memory valid OT metric versus cubic Wasserstein and quadratic non-metric entropic OT.
findings.evidence: Eq. 2 notes Wasserstein O(m^3 log m) time O(m^2) memory; Eq. 3 notes entropic OT O(m^2) time, quadratic memory, not valid metric; Eq. 4 defines SW with O(n log n) time O(n) memory valid metric (Eq. 2, Eq. 3, Eq. 4)

connections.reason: Both apply OT to learned features; bidirectional SW replaces single-direction learned-feature OT energy with bidirectional sliced metric encouraging cycle consistency.
Both use entropy-regularized OT solved by differentiable Sinkhorn projections; prior for training energy, new paper for test-time adaptive refinement.
Bidirectional EBSW with shared slicing distribution is defined as energy-weighted improvement over uniform bidirectional SW.

contributions.what_it_adds: Establishes entropy-regularized OT formulation with squared product-embedding ground cost encoded as Gibbs density, plus a second OT energy using learned-feature distance, providing baseline OT costs against which alternatives can be tested.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: orthogonal - first paper in project with no prior findings to support or challenge; establishes foundational OT cost formulation for shape correspondence.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Partial overlap: paper defines the core squared embedding-distance OT cost and instantiates one alternative ground cost (learned feature distance for initialization in Eq-13 vs geometric embedding distance in Eq-8), but does not systematically compare whether alternative costs improve correspondence.

contributions.what_it_adds: Beyond entropic OT on product embeddings (f1,f2,f4) and learned-feature OT energy (f3), adds bidirectional SW and bidirectional EBSW training losses plus test-time entropic OT Sinkhorn refinement, with direct SHREC19 ablation showing alternatives beat MSE and improve maps.
contributions.stance_toward_prior: supports and extends prior: confirms f3 premise that alternative ground costs on learned features help, while extending beyond f1/f2 entropic OT with quadratic cost and Gibbs density to O(n log n) valid-metric SW/EBSW alternatives.
contributions.overlap_with_direction: Directly explores the direction: defines sliced and energy-based sliced Wasserstein as alternative OT costs, implements them via Monte Carlo/importance sampling, and ablates BiSW/EBSW vs MSE plus entropic refinement for correspondence.
new_open_questions: Do BiSW vs BiEBSW gains persist beyond SHREC19 to SMAL/DT4D-H non-isometric sets?
Can efficient SW training remove need for quadratic-memory entropic Sinkhorn refinement at inference?

open_questions.text: Do alternative OT ground costs beyond squared embedding distance and learned-feature initialization distance improve correspondence quality rather than just alignment tightness?
How do entropy regularization and Gibbs scaling affect correspondence accuracy under different ground costs?
Can learned-feature OT cost replace geometric embedding OT cost throughout alignment, not just for initialization?
Do BiSW vs BiEBSW differences generalize beyond SHREC19 after FAUST+SCAPE training to SMAL/DT4D-H non-isometric sets?
Can SW/EBSW training alone achieve best accuracy without quadratic-memory entropic Sinkhorn refinement at inference?

novelty_risks.direction: Compare alternative OT ground costs (geometric embedding distance vs learned feature distance) to improve non-rigid correspondence
novelty_risks.note: Paper already defines both costs and uses them in the same pipeline (matching vs initialization), so claiming this comparison as entirely novel would overlap.

novelty_risks.direction: Introduce entropy-regularized OT with Gibbs pairwise cost for unsupervised shape matching
novelty_risks.note: Core formulation already established in this paper, so re-proposing it risks duplication.

novelty_risks.direction: Propose sliced or energy-based sliced Wasserstein loss for non-rigid shape correspondence
novelty_risks.note: BiSW and BiEBSW losses already defined and ablated vs MSE; re-proposing same cost risks duplication.

novelty_risks.direction: Propose entropic OT Sinkhorn refinement to improve final correspondence
novelty_risks.note: Entropic OT refinement already shown to improve 4.7 to 7.2 and uses same method as prior entropic OT; repeat work overlaps.
